findings: REAL DEFECT: /writing/51..54 (D-01..D-04) returned HTTP 500 at the 360 AND 768 viewports (i.e. when the dev server was still fresh, not a late-run timeout) with 'Jest worker child process exceptions'. Fresh unauthenticated probe returns HTTP 307 (auth redirect). Likely SSR runtime error when expected question/draft data is absent, or a dev-mode SSR crash. Cascaded into hosted-surface modal IAs (D-M1/D-M2/D-M3) and retry modal (C-03). Fixing is out of audit scope; recorded as a genuine blocking finding (distinct from the degradation noise below).

RUN-INFRASTRUCTURE DEGRADATION (critical for label interpretation): navigation 'page.goto Timeout 15000ms' rows escalated by viewport in run order: 360=1, 768=17, 1280=28 (Playwright runs project-by-project: mobile-360 first while server fresh, desktop-1280 last while server degraded). Post-run idle latency probe: / = 9.8s, /login = 10s, redirects ~5s. Conclusion: most 768/1280 timeouts are dev-server slowdown under sustained load + Next.js dev on-demand compilation, NOT product defects. Pages like A-03/B-01/C-01/X-02/F-01 returned HTTP 200 + rendered + screenshotted at 360 (and often 768) and only timed out at the last viewport.

MERGE CONTAMINATION: merge-ia-audit-results.mjs maps one browser row per IA = the LAST viewport row (1280). Because 28 IA have a 1280 navigation-timeout blockingReason, the mechanical final label is BLOCKED for 28 IA even where 360/768 evidence is clean. The reliable readiness signal is therefore the AI UX review + independent adjudication (which used the clean 360 screenshots + source), not the mechanical merge label. Final report must present both and explain this.

HEURISTIC SUSPECT: B-01, X-02, C-01, C-02 and others were also flagged 'primary CTA regex not visible'; shard reviewers verified several against screenshots and downgraded to PARTIAL/FAIL rather than treating the regex miss as a real blocker.
